symptom: A `create javascript action` whose body uses its own parameters (`Url`, `ReadOnly`) builds cleanly and throws `ReferenceError: Url is not defined` the first time the action runs. `mxcli check` and `mx check` report nothing. After a build the .js signature reads `JS_Open(url, readOnly)` where mxcli wrote `JS_Open(Url, ReadOnly)`, body untouched. A Studio Pro-authored action edited through `create or modify` turns `Geocode(address, ...)` into `Geocode(Address, ...)` over a body that still reads `address`
cause: `GenerateJavaScriptSource` wrote the model parameter name verbatim in the signature and the JSDoc `@param`. mxbuild and Studio Pro regenerate the file from the model, keeping only the user code, EXTRA CODE and imports, and lower-case the first character of each parameter name (only the first: `URL` -> `uRL`, `MyID` -> `myID`, `_Lead` unchanged), so the body was written against identifiers the next build removes
insight: Generated source that a later tool regenerates must follow that tool's naming rule, or the user code inside it breaks silently: it is the user's, so the generator cannot fix it afterwards and nothing between MDL and the click can see it. Measure the rule against the real generator, not against the docs: create an action with awkward names (`URL, MyID, Some_Name, A, XMLData, _Lead, Obj2Name, Eid`), run mxbuild, read what it left (`uRL, myID, some_Name, a, xMLData, _Lead, obj2Name, eid`) - 'camelCase it' would have been wrong for `URL`. Keep the model name (the database keys on it; describe must round-trip) and change only the generated identifier. The earlier finding for the theme switcher worked around this by writing lower-case bodies; the generator was still wrong. Bodies are not rewritten, so a body that uses the declared case still fails: a `check` warning is the separate follow-up. mxbuild also rejects names that differ only in case (`Duplicate parameter name`), which mxcli does not check
